data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The append-only event log requires safe operations, not idempotent ones, because appending is inherently non-idempotent (each append creates a new entry). The log's replay infrastructure enforces idempotency through deduplication (sequence numbers, content hashes, or idempotency keys), so writers only need to be safe: their retries must not corrupt the log or produce inconsistent state. The idempotency burden is on the log infrastructure, not the writers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log lacks any deduplication mechanism, then safe writers will produce duplicate entries and deterministic replay fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If writers can submit events without unique identifiers, the log cannot deduplicate and must rely on writer idempotency.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log's deduplication mechanism is itself non-deterministic (e.g., timing-dependent), it fails to guarantee replay determinism.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A writer submits an event with a unique identifier. The log checks whether an event with that identifier already exists before appending. On retry, the duplicate is silently discarded. The writer's operation (submit event) is safe\u2014resubmission doesn't corrupt state\u2014and the log's deduplication makes the overall system effectively idempotent. This separation of concerns is more robust than requiring every writer to implement idempotency correctly.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
